name: Cauliflower

schedule.notes: Steady moisture and feeding — any stress and heads stay small ('buttoning').
Fall is the easier season; cool ripening = clean white heads.
Cut at the base when curd is 6 to 8 in and tight. Once florets separate, it's past.

harvest.cues: Head is 6 to 8 in across, curds tight. Yellowing means too late.
harvest.storageNotes: Fridge whole 1 week. Blanch florets and freeze for longer.

varieties.name: Graffiti
varieties.notes: Purple curds, no blanching needed. Color fades when cooked.

varieties.name: Cheddar
varieties.notes: Bright orange, 25x the beta-carotene of white. Color holds when cooked.

notes: Tie outer leaves over white-variety heads to blanch (keep them white) once the curd is silver-dollar sized. Purple and orange types don't need blanching.
